title: Question 6
statement_text: Given a polynomial $p$, do there necessarily exist real numbers $c, s \geq 1$ and a positive integer $d$, such that the following holds: every graph $G$ satisfying $\mathrm{col}_r(G) \leq p(r)$ for every non-negative integer $r$ admits a $(c, \sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representation in $\mathbb{R}^d$?
context_text: An intersection representation of a graph $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ assigns to each vertex $v$ a non-empty set $\varphi(v)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for distinct $u,v$, the sets $\varphi(u)$ and $\varphi(v)$ intersect if and only if $uv\in E(G)$; it is $c$-thin if every point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in at most $c$ of the sets $\varphi(v)$. A shape is a compact set not contained in any proper affine subspace. For sets $B_1,B_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ and real $s\ge 1$, write $B_1\sqsubseteq_s B_2$ if for every point $x\in B_2$ there is a translate $B_1'$ of $B_1$ with $x\in B_1'$ and $\mathrm{vol}(B_1'\cap B_2)\ge\frac{1}{s}\mathrm{vol}(B_1)$; $B_1$ and $B_2$ are $\sqsubseteq_s$-comparable if $B_1\sqsubseteq_s B_2$ or $B_2\sqsubseteq_s B_1$. A representation $\varphi$ is $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame if it is $c$-thin, every $\varphi(v)$ is a convex shape, and $\varphi(u),\varphi(v)$ are $\sqsubseteq_s$-comparable for all $u,v$. For a linear ordering $\prec$ of $V(G)$, a path from $v$ to $x$ respects $\prec$ if $v\prec z$ for all its internal vertices $z$; $L_{G,\prec,r}(v)$ is the set of vertices $x\preceq v$ joined to $v$ by a $\prec$-respecting path of length at most $r$; $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)=\max_v|L_{G,\prec,r}(v)|$, and the strong coloring number $\mathrm{col}_r(G)$ is the minimum of $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)$ over all linear orderings $\prec$. The authors prove that for all $c,s\ge1$ and $d$ there is $\delta$ such that if $G$ has a $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representation $\varphi$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, then ordering the vertices by non-increasing volume of $\varphi(v)$ gives $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)\le\delta r^d$ for every $r$ (hence such graphs have balanced separators of size $O(n^{1-1/(2d+4)})$). This parallels the theorem of Krauthgamer and Lee: for every polynomial $p$ there is $d$ such that every graph $G$ whose growth is bounded by $p$ (every ball of radius $r$ has at most $p(r)$ vertices) has an injection $\varphi:V(G)\to\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $\|\varphi(u)-\varphi(v)\|_\infty=1$ for every edge $uv$, which characterizes classes of polynomial growth. A positive answer to the question would give a similar rough geometric characterization of graphs with polynomially bounded strong coloring numbers. The authors suspect that the answer is negative.
notes: The notation $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame and $\sqsubseteq_s$ are rendered as '(cid:118)s' in the PDF extraction; interpreted as the paper's comparability relation defined via volume overlap.
paper_title: Sublinear separators in intersection graphs of convex shapes

title: Informal conjecture: negative answer to Question 6
statement_text: There exists a polynomial $p$ such that for all real numbers $c,s\ge 1$ and every positive integer $d$, some graph $G$ satisfying $\mathrm{col}_r(G)\le p(r)$ for every non-negative integer $r$ does not admit a $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representation in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
context_text: An intersection representation of a graph $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ assigns to each vertex $v$ a non-empty set $\varphi(v)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ such that, for distinct $u,v$, the sets $\varphi(u)$ and $\varphi(v)$ intersect if and only if $uv\in E(G)$; it is $c$-thin if every point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in at most $c$ of the sets $\varphi(v)$. A shape is a compact set not contained in any proper affine subspace. For sets $B_1,B_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ and real $s\ge 1$, write $B_1\sqsubseteq_s B_2$ if for every point $x\in B_2$ there is a translate $B_1'$ of $B_1$ with $x\in B_1'$ and $\mathrm{vol}(B_1'\cap B_2)\ge\frac{1}{s}\mathrm{vol}(B_1)$; $B_1$ and $B_2$ are $\sqsubseteq_s$-comparable if $B_1\sqsubseteq_s B_2$ or $B_2\sqsubseteq_s B_1$. A representation $\varphi$ is $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame if it is $c$-thin, every $\varphi(v)$ is a convex shape, and $\varphi(u),\varphi(v)$ are $\sqsubseteq_s$-comparable for all $u,v$. For a linear ordering $\prec$ of $V(G)$, a path from $v$ to $x$ respects $\prec$ if $v\prec z$ for all its internal vertices $z$; $L_{G,\prec,r}(v)$ is the set of vertices $x\preceq v$ joined to $v$ by a $\prec$-respecting path of length at most $r$; $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)=\max_v|L_{G,\prec,r}(v)|$, and the strong coloring number $\mathrm{col}_r(G)$ is the minimum of $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)$ over all linear orderings $\prec$. The authors prove that $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representability in $\mathbb{R}^d$ implies $\mathrm{col}_r(G)\le\delta r^d$ for all $r$, with $\delta$ depending on $c,s,d$, and asked whether, for every polynomial $p$, there exist $c,s\ge1$ and $d$ such that every graph with $\mathrm{col}_r(G)\le p(r)$ for all $r$ admits a $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame representation in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and write that they suspect the answer is negative. Their evidence: by analogy with the Krauthgamer–Lee embedding of graphs of polynomial growth into $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (a product of maps to a path) one could hope for a representation by boxes (products of $d$ closed intervals), but they prove that for all $c,s\ge1$, every $d$ and every non-decreasing unbounded $f:\mathbb{N}\to[3,+\infty)$, there is a graph $G$ with an ordering $\prec$ such that $\mathrm{col}_{\prec,r}(G)\le f(r)$ for every $r$ which has no $(c,\sqsubseteq_s)$-tame intersection representation in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by boxes.
notes: Stated as suspicion in prose ('we suspect'); Theorem 7 provides partial supporting evidence by ruling out box-shaped tame representations, but the full Question 6 remains open. PDF source — math notation may be garbled.
